privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.contact: If you have any questions about this privacy policy, please contact us:
privacy.section1Content: BudgetWise ("we", "our", "us") is committed to protecting the privacy of our users. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, store, and protect your personal information when you use the BudgetWise application (the "Application"). This policy is designed to comply with the Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA) and Quebec's Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector (Law 25).
privacy.section2Content:
We collect the following types of personal information:

• Account information: email address, name, and encrypted password.
• Financial data: bank account details, transaction history, account balances, and budget information obtained through your connected financial institutions via the Plaid service.
• Usage data: application preferences, consent records, and audit logs of account activity.
• Authentication data: session tokens and two-factor authentication configuration.

We only collect information that is necessary for the operation of the Application.
privacy.section3Content:
We collect your information through:

• Direct input: when you create an account and configure your settings.
• Plaid integration: when you connect your bank accounts, financial data is retrieved through Plaid's secure API. Plaid's own privacy policy governs their data handling practices.
• Automatic collection: session and audit data generated through your use of the Application.

We obtain your explicit consent before collecting, using, or disclosing your personal information. You may withdraw consent at any time through the Privacy & Consent settings.
privacy.section4Content:
Your personal information is used for the following purposes:

• Providing the Application's core features: displaying your financial accounts, transactions, budgets, and reports.
• Authentication and security: verifying your identity and protecting your account.
• Categorization: automatically and manually organizing your transactions.
• Data export: allowing you to export your financial data in CSV or JSON format.

We do not use your information for advertising, marketing to third parties, or any purpose beyond operating the Application.
privacy.section5Content:
Your data is stored in a secure database with the following protections:

• Passwords are hashed using industry-standard algorithms and are never stored in plain text.
• Authentication tokens are cryptographically generated and have defined expiration periods.
• Two-factor authentication (TOTP) is available for additional account security.
• Access to the database is restricted and protected by server-level security measures.
• Data is isolated per user — you can only access your own data.

We retain your data only for as long as necessary to provide the Application's services or as required by law.
privacy.section6Content:
We do not sell, rent, or trade your personal information to third parties.

Your financial data is shared with Plaid Technologies, Inc. solely for the purpose of connecting to your financial institutions. No other third-party sharing occurs.

We may disclose your information if required by law, court order, or governmental regulation.
privacy.section7Content:
Under PIPEDA and Quebec Law 25, you have the following rights:

• Right of access: You may request access to the personal information we hold about you.
• Right of rectification: You may request correction of inaccurate information.
• Right of deletion: You may request the deletion of your personal data. The Application provides a secure data deletion feature in Settings that permanently removes all your financial data (transactions, accounts, connections, budgets, and rules).
• Right to withdraw consent: You may withdraw your consent for data collection, processing, or storage at any time through the Privacy & Consent settings. Withdrawal of certain consents may limit your ability to use specific features.
• Right to data portability: You may export your data at any time using the built-in export feature.
• Right to file a complaint: You may file a complaint with the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada or the Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec.
privacy.section8Content:
The Application implements a granular consent management system:

• Cookie consent: You may accept or decline cookies when first accessing the Application.
• Data collection consent: Controls whether the Application can connect to and synchronize data from your bank accounts.
• Data processing consent: Controls whether the Application can process your data for dashboard and reporting features.
• Data storage consent: Controls whether the Application stores your financial data. Revoking storage consent triggers a secure deletion process.

You can manage all consent preferences at any time in the Privacy & Consent section of Settings.
privacy.section9Content:
In the event of a data breach that poses a real risk of significant harm, we will:

• Notify affected users as soon as feasible.
• Notify the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada.
• Notify the Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec.
• Keep a record of the breach as required by law.
privacy.section10Content:
For any questions, concerns, or requests regarding your personal information, you may contact our Privacy Officer:

BudgetWise
1234 rue de l'Église, Lévis (QC) H0H0H0
Email: budgetwise@guisset.ca

We will respond to your request within 30 days, as required by law.
privacy.section11Content: The Application is not intended for use by individuals under the age of 14. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children. If we become aware that a child under 14 has provided us with personal information, we will take steps to delete that information.
privacy.section12Content: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. Any changes will be reflected in the "Last updated" date at the top of this policy. We encourage you to review this policy periodically. Continued use of the Application after changes constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.

securityPolicy.title: Information Security Policy
securityPolicy.contact: For questions regarding this Information Security Policy, please contact:
securityPolicy.section1Content:
BudgetWise is committed to protecting the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of all information assets entrusted to us by our users. This Information Security Policy (ISP) establishes the framework for our information security program and defines the principles, responsibilities, and standards that govern how we protect sensitive data.

Our objectives are to:

• Protect user financial data and personal information from unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, or destruction.
• Ensure the availability and reliability of the BudgetWise application and its supporting infrastructure.
• Comply with applicable laws and regulations, including PIPEDA and Quebec's Law 25.
• Maintain user trust through transparent and responsible data handling practices.
• Continuously improve our security posture through regular reviews and updates.
securityPolicy.section2Content:
This policy applies to:

• All information assets managed by the BudgetWise application, including user account data, financial transaction records, bank connection credentials, budget configurations, and audit logs.
• All technical infrastructure supporting the application, including web servers, databases, APIs, and third-party integrations (e.g., Plaid).
• All individuals with access to BudgetWise systems, including administrators and end users.
• All environments: production, staging, and development.

This policy covers data at rest, data in transit, and data in processing within the BudgetWise ecosystem.
securityPolicy.section3Content:
Clear accountability is essential to an effective security program. The following roles and responsibilities are established:

• Application Owner / Administrator: Responsible for the overall security of the BudgetWise application, including maintaining this policy, managing user access, monitoring the audit log, and responding to security incidents. Administrators have elevated privileges and are accountable for their responsible use.
• Users: Responsible for maintaining the security of their own credentials, enabling two-factor authentication when possible, and reporting any suspicious activity. Users must not share their login credentials or authentication tokens.
• Third-Party Providers (Plaid): Subject to their own security policies and contractual obligations. BudgetWise selects third-party providers that maintain appropriate security standards and certifications.

All security responsibilities are documented and reviewed during each policy update cycle.
securityPolicy.section4Content:
BudgetWise implements robust authentication and access control measures:

• Password Security: All passwords are hashed using industry-standard bcrypt algorithms. Passwords are never stored in plain text. Users are encouraged to use strong, unique passwords.
• Two-Factor Authentication (2FA): Optional TOTP-based two-factor authentication is available for all users. 2FA adds a second layer of verification using a time-based one-time password generated by an authenticator app. One-time recovery codes are provided during 2FA setup.
• Session Management: Authentication tokens are cryptographically generated, stored securely, and have defined expiration periods. Sessions are invalidated upon logout.
• Role-Based Access: Administrative functions (user management, Plaid configuration, audit log review) are restricted to users with the administrator role. Standard users can only access their own data.
• Audit Logging: All authentication events (successful logins, failed attempts, 2FA changes, password changes) are recorded in the audit log with timestamps, IP addresses, and user agent information.
securityPolicy.section5Content:
BudgetWise employs multiple layers of data protection:

• Data Isolation: Each user's data is logically isolated. API endpoints enforce user-scoped queries, ensuring users can only access their own financial data.
• Encryption in Transit: All communications between the user's browser and the BudgetWise server are encrypted using TLS (HTTPS).
• Database Security: Access to the database is restricted to the application layer. Direct database access is not available to end users.
• Sensitive Data Handling: Plaid access tokens and API credentials are stored securely and are never exposed to the client-side application.
• Data Minimization: We only collect and retain data necessary for the application's functionality. No data is collected for advertising or third-party marketing purposes.
securityPolicy.section6Content:
In the event of a security incident, BudgetWise follows a structured response process:

• Detection: Security events are monitored through the audit log system. Unusual patterns (e.g., repeated failed login attempts, unauthorized access attempts) are flagged for review.
• Assessment: Upon detection, the administrator assesses the scope and severity of the incident to determine if user data has been compromised.
• Containment: Immediate actions are taken to contain the incident, which may include revoking sessions, disabling compromised accounts, or temporarily restricting access.
• Notification: If a breach poses a real risk of significant harm, affected users, the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada, and the Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec are notified as required by law.
• Recovery: Systems are restored to normal operation and additional safeguards are implemented to prevent recurrence.
• Documentation: All incidents are documented with a record of actions taken, findings, and remediation steps.
securityPolicy.section7Content:
BudgetWise integrates with Plaid Technologies, Inc. for bank account connectivity. The following security considerations apply:

• Plaid is SOC 2 Type II certified and maintains comprehensive security controls.
• BudgetWise communicates with Plaid exclusively through their secure API using encrypted connections.
• Plaid access tokens are stored server-side and are never exposed to the client application.
• Users can disconnect their bank connections at any time, which revokes the associated Plaid access tokens.
• BudgetWise supports both Plaid Sandbox and Production environments, with clear separation between test and live data.

No other third-party services have access to user financial data.
securityPolicy.section8Content:
Users have full control over their data within BudgetWise:

• Data Export: Users can export their financial data at any time in CSV or JSON format.
• Data Deletion: Users can securely delete all their financial data (transactions, accounts, connections, budgets, and categorization rules) through the Settings page. This action requires password confirmation.
• Consent Management: Users can manage granular consent preferences for data collection, processing, and storage. Revoking consent triggers appropriate data handling actions.
• Account Security: Users can change their password, enable or disable two-factor authentication, and monitor their account activity through the audit log (administrators).

These controls ensure compliance with the right of access, rectification, deletion, and portability as required by PIPEDA and Quebec Law 25.
securityPolicy.section9Content:
This Information Security Policy is a living document and is subject to regular review:

• Annual Review: This policy is reviewed at least once per year to ensure it remains current and effective.
• Trigger-Based Updates: The policy is updated whenever there are significant changes to the application architecture, new regulatory requirements, or following a security incident.
• Version Control: All changes to this policy are tracked with a revision date. Previous versions are archived for reference.
• Approval: This policy is approved by the BudgetWise application owner. Any substantive changes require review and re-approval before taking effect.

The "Last updated" date at the top of this document reflects the most recent revision.
securityPolicy.section10Content:
BudgetWise is designed to comply with the following regulatory frameworks:

• Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA): Canada's federal private-sector privacy law.
• Quebec's Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector (Law 25): Quebec's provincial privacy legislation, including requirements for privacy impact assessments, incident reporting, and consent management.

This Information Security Policy, together with our Privacy Policy, forms the foundation of our compliance program. We are committed to adapting our practices as regulatory requirements evolve.
